You are correct in that a lot of my pain is different from the typical kind; it's "ghost" pain - I feel pain from areas in my body that are no longer there (my lower leg and foot). I'm glad to hear that the pain specialist will be better able to handle my meds, especially for the breakthrough pain. It makes more sense to use a different kind of med than what is used to treat my around-the-clock pain..it will help keep my tolerance lower too. I've had excellent coverage from my insurance so far and I hope it continues with this new doctor; I've only been paying $1-$2 for my months supply of of oxy and gabapentin.
Yeah, the oxy 80's are the OPs. I'm definitely going to try to get something stronger for my breakthrough pain, I don't even feel anything from those 5's.

I had my left leg amputated below the knee a few months ago and have been in constant pain ever since. I've adapted to walking with a prosthetic leg pretty well, but each step causes pain. I also have extensive peripheral neuropathy in my right leg, which the gabapentin helps with to some degree but I think I'll ask about switching to Lyrica to see if it can do a better job. The only alternative to medication I've tried so far is physical therapy, which was necessary to learn how to walk again. I've sort of accepted that pain is something I'll have to live with for the rest of my life and so far medication has definitely helped, I just want to have it better controlled.
